qualifier: Jupiter sets no minimum seawall height. It caps new bulkheads at the property's FEMA base flood elevation, and a bulkhead more than 3 ft above mean high water must be fully faced with riprap or mangroves.
detail_rows: Minimum :: None set in Sec. 27-2624 (Shoreline stabilization) | Maximum :: Top of new bulkhead must be at or below the property's required base flood elevation on current FEMA maps - Sec. 27-2624(8) | Exemptions to max :: Properties east of the Coastal Construction Control Line; Riverwalk properties where ADA slope cannot be met - Sec. 27-2624(8)a-b | Riprap trigger :: Top more than 3 ft above mean high water line requires 100% riprap/mangrove facing - Sec. 27-2624(1)c, (2)d | Location :: Replacement within 18 in. waterward of existing permitted bulkhead (one-time waterward move since 6/16/2015) - Sec. 27-2624(1)-(2)
source: Town of Jupiter Code of Ordinances, Ch. 27 Zoning, Art. XI Div. 25 Marine Facilities, Sec. 27-2624 (Supp. 24, online 10/2/2026)
notes: No minimum found. Also read Sec. 25-268 (seawalls along access waterways: permit + water-side face on property line; no elevation). Full-text Municode search for seawall/bulkhead returned no other elevation rule. Code text gives no datum; it ties the max to BFE. (The Town building-dept seawall checklist asks for cap elevation in NAVD, but that checklist is not code.)

qualifier: West Palm Beach's zoning code sets no minimum or maximum seawall height. Its shoreline rules cover where walls go and require riprap or vegetation with replacement bulkheads, not elevation.
detail_rows: Minimum :: None set - Ch. 94 Sec. 94-378(b) Shoreline stabilization covers hardening only | Replacement bulkheads :: Must consist of or include sloping rip-rap or permeable materials combined with vegetation - Sec. 94-378(b)(4) | Docks vs. seawall :: No portion of a dock may extend above the top of the bulkhead it is attached to - Sec. 94-313 | Setback :: 15 ft from seawall on tidal waterfront lots - Sec. 94-305
source: City of West Palm Beach Code, Ch. 94 Zoning and Land Development Regulations (enCodePlus), Secs. 94-378, 94-313, 94-305
notes: Chapters 18 and 94 are maintained on enCodePlus (not Municode). Full text of Ch. 94 and Ch. 18 scanned for seawall/bulkhead/NAVD/NGVD: no seawall elevation rule. Municode full-text search of remaining chapters found no elevation rule.

qualifier: New and substantially rebuilt seawalls in North Palm Beach need a cap at least 4 ft NAVD88, or 5 ft NAVD88 on the Intracoastal, Lake Worth or the ocean in a FEMA flood zone. Repairs under 50% of replacement cost are exempt.
detail_rows: Zone X / X500 :: Min 4 ft NAVD88; max 6 in. above grade or 4.5 ft NAVD88, whichever is greater - Sec. 5-72(3) | FEMA SFHA/CHHA with BFE :: Min 4 ft NAVD88; max 6 in. above grade or 5 ft NAVD88, whichever is greater - Sec. 5-72(3) | SFHA/CHHA on Intracoastal, Lake Worth or Atlantic :: Min 5 ft NAVD88; max 6 in. above grade or 6 ft NAVD88, or up to BFE with approved mitigation - Sec. 5-72(3) | Applies to :: New walls and repairs costing 50% or more of replacement cost - Sec. 5-72 | Returns :: Cap above neighbor grade needs a matching wall return - Sec. 5-72(4)
source: Village of North Palm Beach Code, Ch. 5 Boats, Docks and Waterways, Art. III Div. 3, Sec. 5-72 (Ord. 2019-07; Ord. 2026-02, 1-22-26)
notes: Headline 4 is the lowest minimum; 5 ft NAVD88 applies on the Intracoastal/Lake Worth/Atlantic in SFHA/CHHA. Amended 1-22-26.

qualifier: Palm Beach sets no fixed height for seawalls on Lake Worth; the town engineer approves the top based on engineering. Oceanfront bulkheads on the Atlantic bulkhead line must top out at no less than 14.34 ft NGVD 1929.
detail_rows: Lake Worth bulkheads :: Top governed by sound engineering recommendations, approved by town engineer; datum NGVD 1929 - Sec. 62-75(d) | Atlantic Ocean bulkheads/seawalls :: Top not lower than 14.34 ft above mean sea level, NGVD 1929 - Sec. 62-38(b)(3) | Oceanfront raise trigger :: Existing seawall below 14.34 ft NGVD must be raised to min 14.34 ft NGVD with any development of the property - Sec. 66-177 | Maintenance :: PE certification, recertify every 15 years - Sec. 62-77
source: Town of Palm Beach Code, Ch. 62 Marine Structures (Art. II Atlantic Ocean, Art. III Lake Worth), Secs. 62-38, 62-75; Ch. 66 Sec. 66-177
notes: Split answer: 'none' is for Lake Worth (most residential seawalls). Ocean side has a 14.34 ft NGVD29 minimum (Secs. 62-38, 66-177). Datum is NGVD29, not NAVD88 - do not convert. Editor should decide whether headline should show the ocean figure.

qualifier: Palm Beach Gardens' code has no seawall section and sets no seawall height. Seawalls appear only in the floodplain rules and the fertilizer setback.
detail_rows: Minimum :: None found in Code of Ordinances or LDR (Ch. 78) | Floodplain :: Lists bulkheads/seawalls as 'other development' in coastal high hazard areas, no elevation - Ch. 86 Art. III (Sec. 86-137) | Fertilizer :: Measured from top of seawall - Sec. 34-39
source: City of Palm Beach Gardens Code of Ordinances (Municode), Ch. 86 Art. III Floodplain Management; Ch. 78 Land Development
notes: No code chapter specifically governs seawalls. Municode full-text search (seawall, bulkhead, sea wall, tidal flood barrier, seawall elevation/NAVD/NGVD) returned no elevation rule. Confirm with City Engineering before publishing 'none'.

qualifier: Boynton Beach's development code requires a permit for seawalls and keeps the water-side face on the property line, but sets no seawall height.
detail_rows: Minimum :: None set - LDR Ch. 3 Art. V Sec. 3.O | Placement :: Water-side face may not encroach over the property line; no wall east of the 1956 Lake Worth bulkhead line - Sec. 3.O | Related :: Lake Worth landfill must be at least 6 ft above mean sea level (fill, not seawall) - Sec. 3.O | Projection :: Seawalls/docks may not extend more than 1/4 of waterway width - Sec. 3.O
source: City of Boynton Beach Land Development Regulations, Ch. 3 Zoning, Art. V Supplemental Regulations, Sec. 3.O Seawalls, Bulkheads, Docks, and Piers (Gridics CodeHub)
notes: LDR hosted on Gridics CodeHub (linked from Municode). Full LDR text scanned for seawall/bulkhead: no elevation. The 6 ft MSL figure applies to fill, not seawall tops; datum is 'mean sea level per U.S. Government Geodetic Survey'.

qualifier: Highland Beach requires seawalls west of A1A to be at the FEMA base flood elevation or higher. There is no fixed number; it depends on the property's flood map.
detail_rows: West of A1A :: At base flood elevation (BFE) or higher per FEMA FIRM - Sec. 6-128(b) | Cap + dock width :: Combined max 8 ft - Sec. 6-128(b), 30-68(g)(6)b | Oceanfront ridge :: Seawall elevation not less than 16 ft (code says 'above mean sea level', no datum year) - Sec. 6-127(d)(1) | Approval :: Planning board special exception - Secs. 6-127(a), 6-128(a)
source: Town of Highland Beach Code, Ch. 6 Art. V Seawalls; Bulkheads; Retaining Walls, Secs. 6-127, 6-128 (Ord. 2025-002)
notes: Headline is not a number: min = BFE (property-specific). Sec. 30-83(d)(3)b separately says oceanfront seawall finish elevation 'consistent with applicable state requirements' - may conflict with 6-127(d)(1) 16 ft; flag for review.

qualifier: New, substantially repaired or substantially rehabilitated seawalls in Ocean Ridge must have a top (including cap) of at least 5 ft NAVD88. Atlantic Ocean frontage is excluded.
detail_rows: Minimum :: Top elevation incl. cap min 5 ft NAVD88 - Sec. 64-82(a)(1) | Trigger :: New wall, work on more than 50% of shoreline length, or over 50% of replacement cost - Sec. 64-82(c)(5) | Also triggered :: Substantial damage/improvement of the principal structure - Sec. 64-82(b) | Excluded :: Properties adjacent to the Atlantic Ocean - Sec. 64-82(f) | Maximum :: None set
source: Town of Ocean Ridge Code, Ch. 64 Zoning, Art. IV, Sec. 64-82 (Ord. 2025-03, 6-2-2025)

qualifier: Gulf Stream sets no minimum seawall height. It caps new or replacement seawalls on Intracoastal-connected water at 8 ft NGVD (or the NAVD equivalent).
detail_rows: Minimum :: None set | Maximum :: No greater than 8 ft NGVD or its equivalent in NAVD - Sec. 70-78 | Seawall required :: Owners on tidal/brackish water must bulkhead their frontage (not ocean) - Sec. 52-26 | Plans :: Town commission approval - Sec. 52-27
source: Town of Gulf Stream Code, Ch. 70 Art. IV Sec. 70-78 Seawall height; Ch. 52 Art. II Seawalls, Bulkheads, Etc. (Ord. 22-9, 10-28-22)
notes: Datum written as 'NGVD or its equivalent in NAVD' - keep NGVD as primary; do not convert.

qualifier: Manalapan requires a permit and fixed wall lines for seawalls but sets no seawall height.
detail_rows: Minimum :: None set - Ch. 155 Coastal Structures, Secs. 155.60-155.64 | Location :: Ocean seawalls on the adopted sea wall line - Secs. 155.45-155.49; Lake Worth bulkhead/fill line - Secs. 155.30-155.33 | Maintenance :: Seawalls must be kept impervious to sand, built to applicable codes - Sec. 155.64
source: Town of Manalapan Code, Title XV Ch. 155 Beaches and Waterways (Municode)
notes: Only elevation in Ch. 155 is an 8.5 ft above mean sea level beach sand contour (Sec. 155.01), not a seawall height.

qualifier: New and substantially rebuilt seawalls in Tequesta need a cap of at least 4 ft NAVD88. Repairs under 50% of replacement cost are exempt.
detail_rows: Zone X / X500 :: Min 4 ft NAVD88; max 6 in. above grade or 4.5 ft NAVD88, whichever is greater - Sec. 76-33(3) | FEMA SFHA/CHHA with BFE :: Min 4 ft NAVD88; max 6 in. above grade or 5 ft NAVD88, whichever is greater - Sec. 76-33(3) | Applies to :: New walls and repairs of 50% or more of replacement cost - Sec. 76-33 | Returns/drainage :: Cap above neighbor grade needs wall return and drainage plan - Sec. 76-33(4) | Riprap/mangroves :: 100% facing on new/replaced walls - Sec. 76-34
source: Village of Tequesta Code, Ch. 76 Waterway Control, Art. IV, Sec. 76-33 (Ord. 8-24, 11-14-2024)

qualifier: South Palm Beach sets no fixed seawall height. A new seawall or bulkhead cap must match the caps on neighboring properties as far as possible.
